summary: Spark executor retry causes duplicate external webhook invocations when using Python SDK function-calling
description:
Issue summary:
Customer DataFlux is running a large distributed ETL job on Spark (EMR) where each task calls an external HTTP webhook via a Redwood function-call (Python SDK). After intermittent executor preemptions/retries, they observed duplicate webhook deliveries for the same logical ETL record.

Impact:
Duplicate external side effects (webhook POST) causing downstream duplicate records in customer DB. Frequency ~1-3% of tasks under heavy cluster churn. This is customer-facing and breaks idempotency assumptions in their downstream pipeline.

Environment:
- DataFlux environment: prod cluster on AWS EMR (Spark 3.4)
- Python SDK version reported: 2.3.1
- SDK usage pattern: Spark task constructs a FunctionCallRequest with tool info, relies on SDK to inject idempotency metadata (no explicit idempotency_key passed by caller)
- Deployment: Dedicated Redwood tenant in us-east-1; function invokes external webhook over HTTP 200 path

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1. Submit Spark job that maps 1M small records across many executors; each map executes a Redwood function call that triggers external POST.
2. During run, preempt an executor (kill -9) to force Spark retry.
3. Observe webhook logs for duplicate POSTs with different Redwood request ids but same logical ETL record id contained in body.

Observed logs/snippets provided by customer:
- SDK client logs: "INFO funcall: sending request id=rc-7a3b..." then later "INFO funcall: sending request id=rc-9f2c..." for same record_id=abc-123
- Webhook server received two POSTs within 2s: payload.record_id=abc-123
- Redwood serving logs show two separate requests; no explicit idempotency_key present in headers

Initial hypothesis:
- Spark serializes the user code and the SDK context when moving tasks across executors. Redwood SDK previously relied on a per-process/thread-local idempotency token generated at call-time. If that token lived in thread-local or non-serializable state, it may be regenerated on the retried executor, causing a new idempotency key and thus a duplicate external call.

Investigation notes (support):
- Reproduced locally with a small Spark (local mode) job: when a worker process is killed and the task is retried, SDK-generated ephemeral idempotency metadata was different on retry.
- Confirmed Python SDK v2.3.1 stores idempotency context in threading.local and sometimes in-memory cache not preserved across process restart/serialization.
- Looked at server-side dedupe: Redwood currently dedupes on explicit idempotency-key header; without explicit key, two different requests are treated as separate.
- Correlated with reported GitHub issue and found similar pattern in PR discussion: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/475 (context about explicit_idempotency option)

Customer impact mitigation recommended to customer:
1) Short-term workaround (immediate): Pass an explicit deterministic idempotency_key in the function call payload/metadata. Suggested pattern: f"dataflux:{job_id}:{record_id}". This key survives retries because customer code constructs and passes it explicitly.
2) Alternative immediate: Upgrade to SDK v2.4.3 (see related PR) which exposes explicit_idempotency parameter and documents serialization-friendly helpers.
3) Server-side mitigation (for customer): Request that webhook consumers dedupe on record_id field in payload as a defensive measure if feasible.

Actions taken by Support/SRE:
- Provided a small repro repo and Spark job that demonstrates the issue and confirms duplicate POSTs when relying on SDK ephemeral idempotency. Link shared: https://github.com/redwood-cases/spark-funcall-repro
- Validated that upgrading to v2.4.3 with explicit_idempotency fixes repro locally when using deterministic idempotency keys.
- Opened a follow-up internal task to improve SDK docs for distributed runtimes (INT-1942).
- Raised a minor server enhancement request to better detect probable-duplicate payloads when explicit idempotency header is missing (tracked separately).

Resolution summary:
- Root cause: reliance on ephemeral, non-serialized idempotency token inside Python SDK which does not survive Spark executor retry/serialization. Retries resulted in regenerated idempotency tokens and therefore duplicate external webhook invocations.
- Fix/workaround: Customer implemented explicit deterministic idempotency_key derived from job_id+record_id and rolled to production; duplicates stopped. We recommended an SDK upgrade to v2.4.3 which documents and exposes helpers for the distributed-use-case.

Follow-ups / action items:
- SDK Docs: add "Using Redwood SDK in distributed environments (Spark/Kubernetes)" with examples for explicit idempotency keys and Spark-safe patterns (owner: DevEx).
- SDK: consider making explicit_idempotency helper the recommended default or add a warning when thread-local idempotency is used in long-running/distributed processes (owner: SDK team).
- Runbook: add an entry under function-calling runbook for "Spark/EMR retries causing duplicate side effects" (owner: Support).
comments: 2026-03-10 11:12 UTC - Ava Reynolds: Initial triage completed. Reproduced in local Spark mode. Asking SRE to confirm server-side dedupe behavior.
2026-03-10 13:04 UTC - Marco Li (SRE): Server dedupe only uses explicit idempotency-key header. No additional heuristics. We can consider payload-based heuristics but that risks false positives.

2026-03-11 09:20 UTC - Customer (J. Patel, DataFlux): Implemented explicit idempotency_key=f\"dataflux:{job_id}:{record_id}\" and observed no duplicates in next run. Thanks for the pattern suggestion.
2026-03-11 14:05 UTC - Diego Martinez: Created PR to expose explicit_idempotency helper and documented pattern in SDK examples. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/482
2026-03-12 08:30 UTC - Support (Ava): Marking resolved; customer confirmed workaround in prod. Filing follow-up tasks INT-1942 and docs update ticket.
2026-03-12 10:00 UTC - Product (Lena Korhonen): Noted as product input for SDK behavior in distributed contexts; will prioritize docs and consider SDK UX change in next sprint.
resolution: Workaround implemented by customer: pass deterministic explicit idempotency_key (job_id+record_id). Recommended upgrade to python-sdk v2.4.3 which exposes explicit helpers. Follow-up docs and internal SDK UX task opened.
